Presidential Gubernatorial Dr Ambassador Rebecca Godwin-Isaac, receiving award of excellence from Sen. Orji Uzor Kalu, Founder, Sun Newspapers. Standing beside her is her husband
Dr (Mrs) Rebecca Omokamo Godwin-Isaac, Chief Executive Officer of Homadil Realty Limited and Summit Estate Global Limited, has received The Sun Real Estate Icon Award 2026 in recognition of her contributions to Nigeria’s property sector. Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, founder of The Sun Newspaper and The Sun Publishing Limited, personally presented the award to her at the Expo Convention Centre, Eko Hotels and Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Friday, 13 November 2026.
The ceremony, themed Nation Builders, celebrated Nigerians recognised for leadership, enterprise and service across several fields. In its “post-event report” ( https://thesun.ng/night-of-bliss-splendour-razzmatazz/ ), The Sun confirmed Godwin-Isaac as a recipient of the Real Estate Icon distinction. For her, the occasion was a national acknowledgement of an entrepreneurial journey and the property-development work associated with the businesses she leads.
The recognition had been set in motion before the Lagos ceremony. The Sun’s Managing Director and Editor-in-Chief, Onuoha Ukeh, led a delegation that formally notified Godwin-Isaac of her selection during a visit in Abuja. She welcomed the decision and thanked the newspaper’s Board of Editors, describing the honour as a source of encouragement to continue contributing to the industry.
In its “published profile” ( https://thesun.ng/rebecca-omokamo-godwin-isaac-a-reputation-for-long-term-value-creation/ ), The Sun highlighted her experience in business development, market research and contract negotiation. Her education, as reported by the newspaper, includes degrees from the University of Maiduguri, the National Open University of Nigeria and the University of South Wales, alongside Harvard Business School’s General Management Programme and a doctorate in Real Estate Economics and Finance from American Management University.
The recognition places her among Nigerian women whose professional lives challenge the assumption that property development and large-scale business leadership are predominantly male pursuits. Her emphasis on entrepreneurship, learning and long-term planning also provides a wider context for an award centred on real estate.
Much of her professional work centres on Homadil Realty Limited, which operates in Abuja’s property sector with activities spanning residential development, construction coordination, brokerage and project management.
For homebuyers and investors, those demands extend beyond attractive designs and locations. Title verification, construction standards, transparent terms and delivery timelines are central to responsible real estate development. In an expanding city such as Abuja, developers must align commercial ambition with the practical needs of future residents.

Godwin-Isaac also heads Summit Estate Global Limited, whose residential development at Apo-Dutse has become a visible part of her property-development portfolio. The project illustrates the scale of the planning and coordination involved in creating a new residential community.
The project’s plans moved into the public spotlight when Summit Estate Global held its groundbreaking on 14 February 2026 at Cadastral Zone B14, Apo-Dutse, Abuja. The development is planned to comprise approximately 180 residential units, including detached homes, semi-detached homes and flats, together with supporting facilities. These are proposed development figures, not a statement that the homes have already been completed.
The “News Agency of Nigeria reported” ( https://nannews.ng/shettima-urges-estate-developers-to-uphold-standards-professionalism/ ) that Vice President Kashim Shettima was represented at the groundbreaking by his Senior Special Assistant on Legal and Compliance, Bashir Maidugu. The representative encouraged developers to prioritise proper title documentation, construction quality and professional estate management.
The same report identified JI Construct Limited among the construction firms represented at the event. Rebecca’s husband, Engineer Isaac Ishaku Yusuf, is the Chief Executive Officer of JI Construct Limited, bringing construction and project-management expertise to residential development.
The significance of the Apo-Dutse project ultimately rests on the translation of its plans into a well-managed residential environment, supported by clear documentation, effective construction and reliable communication with purchasers.
Beyond her work in property development, Godwin-Isaac has advocated opportunities for girls and women to gain education, confidence and greater economic independence. Earlier coverage by “The Guardian” ( https://guardian.ng/specials/nigerias-most-impactful-women-in-leadership-2/ ) identified her with The Girl Yesterday, The Woman Today, an initiative associated with mentoring and support for girls and women.
Her advocacy reflects a broader view of success: that commercial enterprise can sit alongside efforts to equip others to pursue their ambitions. The Sun’s recognition brings renewed attention to these interests as well as to her role in Abuja’s real estate industry.
For Rebecca Omokamo Godwin-Isaac, the 2026 award marks an important professional milestone. For Homadil Realty Limited and Summit Estate Global Limited, the enduring measure will be progress that can be independently assessed through responsible development and completed projects. The Lagos ceremony celebrated recognition already earned; the lasting legacy will depend on the communities built and opportunities created in the years ahead.
